references.text: Describes the same principle that a poor person may bring a lesser offering when they cannot afford the usual offering
Shows God's gracious provision for the poor who cannot afford the standard offering
Parallel provision for poor women after childbirth, demonstrating the same principle of reduced offerings for those with limited means
The full offering required from those who can afford it, which this verse provides as an alternative for the poor
Reference to a lamb as an offering, the same type of animal mentioned in this provision for the poor
Describes the guilt offering (אָשָׁם) also mentioned in this verse
Basic regulation concerning the grain offering (מִנְחָה) with fine flour and oil, which is also mentioned here
Paul writes about Christ becoming poor for our sake, a spiritual principle reflecting God's care for the poor in the Mosaic Law
Mary and Joseph brought the poor person's offering after Jesus' birth, showing that they made use of similar provisions for the poor
